paragraphs: R. Yaakov bar Aḥa, a leading sage of the generation alongside Rabbi. In Mo'ed Katan (22b): a leading man whose father died wished to bare his shoulder in mourning—who was he? Rabbi. A leading sage of the generation who was with him wished to bare his shoulder—who was he? R. Yaakov bar Aḥa. Some reverse it. In Shabbat, chapter Bammeh Madlikin (31b): R. Simon and R. Elazar were sitting; one said, 'Let us stand before him, because he is learned in Torah,' and the other said, 'Because he fears sin.' R. Aḥa bar Yaakov appears to be his son. R. Yishmael son of R. Yaakov bar Aḥa [the abbreviation ב״א follows as a separate fragment in the source]. Here are some who spoke in the name of R. Yaakov bar Aḥa; it requires examination whether this is the one who lived in Rabbi's time. I shall therefore write down every R. Yaakov bar Aḥa and bar Rav Aḥa, and afterward set out those who speak in his name; you may discern.
